sentences.text:
The petitioner has filed this petition being aggrieved by the arbitral award passed by the Special Deputy Commissioner/Arbitrator, Bengaluru Urban District, Bengaluru, in No. LAQ / ARB / NH-7 /
CR / 148 / 2012-13 dated 05.01.2021 in respect of Sy. No.67 measuring 750 Sq. Meters of agricultural land of Meenukunte village, Jala Hobli, Bengaluru North Addl. Taluka, Bengaluru Urban District.

. The definite case of the petitioner is that the property bearing Sy. No.67 measuring 750 Sq. Meters situated at Meenukunte village, Jala Hobli has been acquired under Preliminary Notification issued by the respondent No. 2 under Section 3A(1) vide S.O. No.3159 (E)
dated 09.12.2009 and Final Notification under Section 3D(1) and (2) vide S.O. No. 1622(E) dated 02.07.2010.
The respondent No.2 has passed the award on 13.12.2010 and awarded a total compensation amount of Rs.37,06,632/-, which has been received by the petitioner under protest.

Subsequently, on 17.08.2012 the petitioner filed the application stating that the award amount is paid at agricultural rate though land is converted land and hence prayed to enhance the amount at conversion rate and at market rate and also to direct the SLAO and Competent Authority to pay the amount of difference.
Accordingly, the application is taken by the respondent No.3 for consideration.
In the said petition, the respondent No.2 filed statement of objection stating that the contention urged by the petitioner are baseless and the same are made without any substance.
The petitioner has not produced any relevant documents to justify its claim for enhanced compensation and the claim of the petitioner cannot be sustained in law.
Hence, question of enhancement of compensation will not arise and the claim of the petitioner is liable to be dismissed by the respondent No.2.
Accordingly, prayed to dismiss the reference.

Being aggrieved by the impugned Arbitral Award, the petitioner filed this petition under Section 34(2) of the Arbitration and Conciliation Act, 1996, setting up the following :

2 The petitioner claims that the impugned award passed by the respondent No.3 is A.P.
No.120/2022 wholly erroneous, contrary to law, materials on record and in violation of principles of natural justice and the same is liable to be set aside.
The petitioner claims that the respondent No.3 committed a legal misconduct in not following the documents filed by the petitioner for deciding the market value.
The Arbitrator failed to appreciate the fact that the respondent No. 3 has not produced any documents to justify the award passed by him.
The award dated 13.12.2010 passed by the respondent No. 2 is not in accordance with the guidance value under Section 3G(7) of NH Act.
The Arbitrator failed to appreciate the claim of the petitioner and passed an order inappropriately.
The award amount is not at all matching with the market value for prime land of the petitioner.
The land acquired is more than value than the award amount, even the amount awarded.
The respondent No. 3 enhanced just and meager compensation without taken into consideration material evidence placed before the Court, which is against A.P. No.120/2022 probabilities of the case.
The respondent No. 3 grossly erred in considering the fact that the acquired land situated very near to Bengaluru International Airport and situated amidst the lands commercially developed.

The LAO and Arbitrator has not recorded any evidence and not considered for payment of solatium on the award amount and additional market value along with interest from the date of taking possession till the date of payment and among other grounds prayed to set aside the same.
.6.

The respondent No.1 filed a detailed objections claiming that the application is not maintainable either in law or on facts and the respondent No. 3 passed the award as per the guidance value produced before the Arbitrator pertaining to the year 2011.
The petitioner is attempting to mislead this Court by drawing reference to incorrect/wholly inapplicable guidance notification.
The respondent No.1 totally denied all the grounds claimed by the petitioner A.P. No.120/2022 in the petition.

The Arbitrator/ respondent No. 3 passed the award after giving full opportunity of hearing to the petitioner by considering the material evidence on record for enhancement of compensation together with all other statutory benefits available under the LA Act in accordance with law and prayed for dismissal of the petition.
.7. The petitioner along with the petition filed I.A. No. 1 under Section 34(3) of Arbitration and Conciliation Act, for condonation of delay if any filing the petition.

.8. The above application is supported with the affidavit of petitioner, wherein, it is stated that the order has not been communicated to him and when he approached the concerned authority on 18.04.2022, he came to know about the order and he immediately applied for copy of the order and he got the same on 26.05.2022.
In view of non communication of the order there is no delay in filing the appeal.

Further stated that5 the award of the respondent No.3 is passed on A.P. No.120/2022 05.01.2021 and the petitioner received the order copy from the office of the Arbitrator and hence,
the cause of action arises only on 26.05.2022 even though the statutory period of limitation of 90 days is lapsed in filing this suit, the limitations stand extended as per the direction of the Hon'ble Supreme Court and Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka and prayed for condonation of delay if any in filing the petition.

sentences.text: The respondents have not filed any objections to the IA.
.10. The respondent No.1 appeared before the Court through his Advocate.
The respondent No.3 appeared through ADGP.
The respondent No.2 though served with the notice, not chosen to appear before the Court to resist the petition.
The entire records in LAQ/ARB/NH-7/CR.148/2012-13 dated 05.01.2021 secured from the Arbitrator.

.11. On the basis of above, the points for consideration are as under:
A.P. No.120/2022 1) Whether the petition filed by the petitioner is within time ?
2) Whether the impugned award of the Arbitrator/SLAO is against law, fact, evidence and probabilities of the case and liable to be intervened by this Court?
3) What order or award?
.12.
Heard the arguments.

The learned advocate for the petitioner relied on judgments reported in (1) In Civil Appeal No. 7064/2019 (Arising out of SLP (C) No. 9599 of 2019) - Union of India Vs.
Tarsem Singh; (2) In No. SLP (C) No.19775/2021 (2022 LiveLaw (SC) 584) ; (3) SLAO and another Vs. Sri. Muthaiah and another in MFA No. 2930/2020; (4) Sri. B.V. Achuthanandareddy Vs. The Project Director and General Manager and others in A.P. No.126 /2022; (5)NHAI and another Vs.
The Additional Commissioner and others in A.A. No.3/2022 and (6) In Suo Motu Writ petition (Civil) No. 3 of 2020 with respect to Cognizance for Extension of Limitation extending the limitation period of 90 days A.P. No.120/2022 from 01.03.2022.

Perused the materials on record, on that basis my findings on the above points are as under:
Points No.1 & 2 : In the affirmative Point No.3 : As per final order, for the following:
REASONS .13.

POINT NO.1: Perused the I.A. No.1 along with affidavit that has been filed for condonation of delay in filing the petition, satisfied with reasons therein and the said application is not opposed by the respondent No.1.
Accordingly, I am of the humble opinion that the petitioner has made out sufficient grounds to condone the delay in filing the petition.
Accordingly the point No. 1 is answered in the affirmative.
.14. POINT No.2: Before proceeding further in this case, it is relevant to note an admitted and undisputed facts in this case.

The Authorized Signatory of the petitioner namely Gajendra Kumar claimed that the petitioner is an owner of the property bearing Sy. No.67 measuring to an extent of 750 Sq. meters of agricultural A.P. No.120/2022 land (dry) of Meenukunte village, Jala Hobli,
Bengaluru North Additional Taluka and the said property has been acquired for widening of NH-7 under Preliminary Notification dated 09.12.2009 and Final Notification dated 02.07.2010, that has been published in the official Gazette on 02.07.2010, is an admitted fact.

It is also an admitted and undisputed fact in this case that the respondent No.2/Special Land Acquisition and Competent The Hamlet vs The Project Director And General ... on 10 February, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/10971141/
4
Authority of National Highways Authority of India being a SLAO determined the compensation at Rs. 37,06,632/- and the same was disbursed to the petitioner as compensation.

.15. Subsequent to the receipt of compensation or passing of the award, the Authorized Signatory of the petitioner Sri. Gajendra Kumar filed an application on 17.08.2012 before the respondent No.3 claiming that the award amount is paid at agricultural rate though land is converted land and hence prayed to enhance the amount at conversion rate and at market rate and also to direct the SLAO and Competent Authority to pay the A.P. No.120/2022 amount of difference.
On basis of the said application, the respondent No.3 hold an inquiry and passed common order in LAQ/ARB/NH-7/CR-148/2012-2013 dated 05.01.2021.
The respondent No.3 in its order enhanced the compensation at Rs.2,625/- per Sq. feet from Rs. 1,500/- per Sq. feet and awarded additional compensation of Rs.1,125/- per Sq. feet.
.16. The said enhancement has been challenged by the petitioner in this petition.

The grievance of the petitioner is that the respondent No.3 without considering the documentary evidence placed by the petitioner and also without considering the claim of the petitioner that enhanced market value other properties are much higher than the compensation enhanced by the respondent No.3 in respect of the acquired property of the petitioner.
The said claim of the petitioner is also found in the award.

On close perusal of the order passed by the respondent No.3, it is clear that the respondent No.3 considering the guidance value of the year 2010-11 published vide notification bearing No. A.P. No.120/2022 CVC 19/2010-11 dated 21.09.2011 enhanced the compensation, but there is no material on record to show that the petitioner has produced the alleged documents claimed by the petitioner in the petition for perusal of Arbitrator/respondent No. 3.
.17.

However, it is the definite case of petitioner that the very same Arbitrator in different cases has enhanced the market value 3 times and such enhancement of compensation not given to the petitioner though the property of the petitioner is acquired for National Highways and the said property of the petitioner was abutting to the National Highways.
.18. In support of this contention, the petitioner has produced the copy of the order passed in LAQ/ARB/NH-07/CR/01/2019-20 dated 09.01.2020.
In the said case, the LAO has enhanced the compensation 3 times of the compensation awarded by LAO/ respondent No. 2.
Admittedly in the case on hand, the LAO awarded the compensation of Rs.1,500/- per Sq. feet and it is enhanced to the tune of Rs.2,625/- per A.P. No.120/2022 Sq. feet by enhancing only Rs.1,125/-.
Therefore, the claim of the petitioner is probable that the respondent No.3 has not properly appreciated the material placed before him while passing the order.
Apart from that, the impugned order of the respondent No. 3 also does not disclose any reasons for the enhancement made in the impugned award.
The Arbitrator has stated much about contention taken by petitioner and respondent No. 1 in the order and abruptly decided the market value without assigning any proper reasons.
Hence, the order of the LAO certainly liable to be intervened by this court.
Accordingly, the point No.2 is held in the affirmative.
.19. Point No.3: In view of my above finding, I proceed to pass the following.
